title: Madisonville music teachers and local musicians
summary: Ernie recalls Professor Divergis, who taught poor youngsters for little or nothing around the north shore, and the small local groups there. His brother studied with him too.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And you know Tommy Ladner over there, was that before your time?
No, I didn't know Tommy Ladner.
Well we're thinking of other people over there, did you ever...

I'll tell you who I did see over there, there was a man by the name of Professor Divergis. He was something like pinch back at that time, would go around teaching youngsters that didn't quite have enough means to go to school. And they had another group of fellas in Madisonville, it was Joe Clark who played the violin, his daddy played the bass, and Joe, let's see what this guy's name, he was a high school, he played trombone. And then Paul Santon was a guitar player, well he taught them, there was about six of them.
The Voidners taught mostly scholars for nothing.
That's right, that's what he did.
Was that Charlie Divergis, who's named Charlie? Yeah.
I have to know, Jerry's a professor and never studied from him when he was in jail.

He's from here, he's from New Orleans, but he would come to Madisonville and go to Manderville, it'd be the spring at Covington, to all the schools, and donate most of each time to teach music to young students. My brother went to him too.
Well when you started on drums, did you say you had your own set, they had a couple sets in the band?
No, my brother had two sets and he would leave a set and he would go out with the other.
